title: Chubb rejects former Australia chief Ben Howell’s claims after forensic review
full_text:
Chubb has told Insurance Business that it commissioned an independent external forensic accounting review after receiving claims brought by its former country president for Australia and New Zealand, and that the review found the claims had no substance.
"Chubb takes all such claims seriously," a Chubb spokesperson said in an emailed statement. "Therefore, upon these claims being received, Chubb initiated an independent external forensic accounting review. This investigation found that the claims are without merit. We are vigorously defending these claims."
It is the insurer's first substantive comment on the proceedings. When the action was filed in the federal court in October, Chubb said only that it would be inappropriate to comment while the matter was before the court.
Ben Howell, who led Chubb's general insurance business in Australia and New Zealand until April 2026, lodged a general protections claim under the Fair Work Act in the Federal Court's New South Wales registry in October. Chubb Insurance Australia Limited is the lead respondent, and 11 individuals are also named, as Insurance Business reported when the proceedings were first filed.
Read next: Former Chubb Australia chief takes insurer and board to Federal Court
Howell's statement of claim is reported to allege that Chubb recognised written premium when contracts were processed through its internal systems rather than when they became legally enforceable, and that he was dismissed after raising concerns about the effect on reported financial performance. Those details were reported by the Australian Financial Review today.
In a statement issued through his lawyers, Howell said he was not prepared to provide what he described as "false financial narratives".
Chubb rejects the allegations, as set out in its statement above. None of the allegations has been tested in court. Chubb and the individual respondents have not yet filed defences and the court file lists only documents filed by Howell.
Howell is represented by Harmers Workplace Lawyers.
The case is an example of a senior executive naming individual managers and directors alongside a corporate employer. Under section 550 of the Fair Work Act, a person involved in a contravention may be treated as having committed it, which is the exposure management liability and employment practices wordings are written to respond to.

Chubb's Australian leadership has been in transition since April, with Chris Colahan appointed interim country president.
